sources.news_title: Darline Graham: 'I'm In'
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham isn't treating her late brother's Senate seat as a short-term assignment after all. The South Carolina Republican, appointed last week to succeed Sen. Lindsey Graham, said in a Fox News interview Monday that she has decided to run for the seat in the special GOP primary. "I'm in," she told host Sean Hannity, who noted that she would have to file to run before her brother's funeral has taken place. 
 -  Graham said she felt an "inner peace" about the decision. "I have been praying a lot, talking to my family. But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I'm a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey," she said. 
 
                            
                            
                            
                            
                            
                                
                                
                                    
                                        Her appointment was initially viewed as a stopgap move that would end in January, but President Trump declared Friday that he would back her if she jumped into the race, adding, "RUN, DARLINE, RUN!" The special election primary is set for Aug. 11, with the candidate filing period opening Tuesday and closing a week later. Graham will face a Republican field that already includes Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman, Politico reports.
                                    
                                
                                
                                
                                
                                
                                    
                                        Under federal rules, only $2,000 of the millions in Lindsey Graham's campaign account can be transferred to his sister's campaign, Bradley A. Smith, a former chairman of the Federal Election Commission, tells the AP. He adds, however, that thanks to a recent Supreme Court decision, the National Republican Senatorial Committee, which can receive an unlimited amount from the late senator's campaign, can "spend an unlimited amount in coordination with Darline's campaign."

sources.news_title: Darline Graham to run for full U.S. Senate term after replacing late brother Lindsey
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham said Monday she’s running for a full term to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham’s Senate seat.
“I’ve made a decision,” Darline Graham told Fox News Channel host Sean Hannity, according to a clip released of an interview set to air later Monday. “I’m in.”
The entrance of Darline Graham – sworn in last week to fulfill the remaining months of her late brother’s term, which expires in January – into the Republican scramble to select a new Senate nominee further complicates an already rushed process following Lindsey Graham ‘s death earlier this month.
A weeklong filing period opens Tuesday for the special Republican primary, which will be Aug. 11. On Friday, President Donald Trump said that Darline Graham had his “Complete and Total Endorsement” to seek the nomination, adding, “RUN, DARLINE, RUN!”
Lindsey Graham’s sister selected to finish his Senate term
Last week, Gov. Henry McMaster appointed Darline Graham to serve the remainder of her brother’s term, which ends in January. In his announcement, McMaster made no reference to Darline Graham as a placeholder or symbolic appointment, although a person familiar with McMaster’s thinking but unauthorized to speak publicly said the governor, in selecting Darline Graham, had never contemplated that she would run for the seat herself.
Before the emergence of Darline Graham – and their Oval Office meeting after she was sworn in – Trump had previously suggested he could back a potential candidacy from Rep. Russell Fry, who said Monday he would officially enter the special primary.
Several other noteworthy politicians, including Rep. Ralph Norman, have already gotten in, and others like Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette have been eyeing a run. Rep. Nancy Mace announced Monday she would not enter the contest.
Darline Graham told Hannity said she had been “praying a lot” about how to navigate her new role.
“It is a tremendous amount of pressure,” she said.
“I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey,” Darline Graham said. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes.”
Funeral services for Lindsey Graham are scheduled to be held next week in Washington and South Carolina. A preliminary report from the medical examiner said he suffered a tear in his aorta.
The millions in Lindsey Graham’s campaign account aren’t funds that Darline Graham could directly access in a run of her own, according to Bradley A. Smith, a former chairman of the Federal Election Commission.
Under federal rules, Lindsey Graham’s campaign would be limited to transferring just US$2,000 to a potential Darline Graham candidacy. However, Smith said there is no limit on how much it could transfer to the National Republican Senatorial Committee, which could – thanks to a Supreme Court decision last month – “spend an unlimited amount in co-ordination with Darline’s campaign.”

sources.news_title: Darline Graham Nordone jumps into South Carolina Senate race for brother’s seat
Darline Graham seeks to succeed brother in US Senate
sources.text:
Senator Darline Graham announced Monday that she will seek a full six-year term representing South Carolina, entering the special Republican primary to succeed her late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham.
“I’ve made a decision. I’m in," Graham said during an interview on Fox News.
Graham, 62, was sworn into the Senate last week after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to complete the remainder of her brother’s term, which ends in early January. She previously worked in disabilities services and most recently served as commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind.
Speaking about her decision, Graham said she had spent time praying and consulting with her family before deciding to run.
“I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey," she said. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes. Absolutely."
President Donald Trump last week publicly encouraged Graham to seek a full term, saying after meeting her at the White House that she would have his “complete and total endorsement."
“I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey," Trump wrote.
The late senator had secured the Republican nomination in June for what would have been his fifth Senate term before his death on July 11. Following his death, the Republican nominee will be selected through a special primary. Candidate filing runs from July 21 through July 28, with the primary scheduled for Aug. 11. If no candidate receives a majority of the vote, a runoff will be held on Aug. 25.
The Republican nominee will face Democrat Annie Andrews in the November general election.
Other Republicans seeking the nomination include Reps. Ralph Norman and Russell Fry.

sources.news_title: Lindsey Graham’s sister intends to run for full-term in the Senate: ‘I’m in’
sources.text:
Lindsey Graham’s sister Darline intends to run for full-term in the Senate: ‘I’m in’
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Add The New York Post on GoogleWASHINGTON — Late Sen. Lindsey Graham’s sister, Darline Graham Nordone, announced that she intends to run for a full six-year term in the Senate.
Nordone (R-SC), who was sworn in as an interim senator last week, reflected on President Trump’s public encouragement for her to run and on the legacy of her brother, who died suddenly at age 71.
“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family,” she told Fox News’ Sean Hannity. “I know I’m a hard worker.”
“He [Lindsey] cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state,” she added. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it.”
“I’ve made a decision,” she concluded. “I’m in.”
The filing deadline for the GOP nod for South Carolina’s Senate seat opens Tuesday, giving the newly minted interim senator just about a week to formalize her bid.
Notably, her decision has to be made before her brother’s funeral on July 28, which had been delayed due to the scores of world leaders and dignitaries who wanted to attend.
The primary will take place on Aug. 11.
The late senator died abruptly on July 11 from heart complications and had been vying for another term in the Senate. South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster (R) promptly tapped Nordone for the seat in a placeholder capacity.
Initially, Nordone was seen as a placeholder for the role, and a handful of Republicans such as Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC) and Ralph Norman (R-SC) began exploring a possible run for the seat. Rep. Russell Fry (R-SC) announced Monday he will enter the race — setting up a potential face-off with Trump’s choice.
Trump publicly implored Nordone to go for the job — just days after McMaster chose her to serve out the final months of Graham’s current term.
“We have known each other for a long time — She is a spectacular person, and a true American Patriot,” Trump wrote on Truth Social last week.
“During her visit, I asked Nordone, for the Good of our Nation, to run for the U.S. Senate in the Special Republican Primary on Tuesday, August 11, 2026. I hope Nordone does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey.”
Nordone’s full interview with Hannity is set to air at 9 p.m. ET Monday.

sources.news_title: Sen. Darline Graham running to keep Lindsey's seat after Trump endorses
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham running to keep brother's seat after Trump endorses
Sen. Darline Graham, who's serving out the remainder of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's term in the Senate, said she will seek a full term for the South Carolina seat her brother held for more than two decades.
"I've made a decision. I'm in," Graham told Fox News anchor Sean Hannity on July 20.
Graham's decision comes days after she received a major endorsement from President Donald Trump as she pondered replacing her older brother, who died July 11.
"RUN, DARLINE, RUN!" Trump said in a July 17 Truth Social post. Graham, 62, "has been a WINNER all of her life and, should she accept, has my Complete and Total Endorsement," the president wrote.
Last month, Lindsey Graham, the longtime senator, prevailed over five primary challengers. Now there will be a special primary election on Aug. 11. Republican candidates must file by July 28 to appear on the ballot. The winner will take on Democrat Annie Andrews in November's midterm election.
The first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. Senate, Graham told Hannity in an interview that she has been discussing with loved ones her decision to run for a full, six-year Senate term.
"I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family. But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey. He cared about the people of this state," Graham said. "I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state. I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it.
"Will it be difficult?" Graham continued. "Yes, absolutely."
Nancy Mace makes a decision
Other Republican candidates who have announced plans to run in the Aug. 11 Republican primary include South Carolina Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman and South Carolina businessman Mark Lynch, who lost to Lindsey Graham in the June Republican primary.
Rep. Nancy Mace said in a July 21 social media post that she's not running for the seat. Mace, who finished last in South Carolina's five-way gubernatorial primary last month, had hinted at running for it in the wake of Graham's death earlier in July.
Initially seen as a placeholder for her brother's seat, Graham has impressed her Senate colleagues.
"She’ll be a principled conservative leader and a strong advocate for South Carolina families," Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Arkansas, said in a July 21 social media post. "She has my full support."
"Why not her?" Graham's South Carolina counterpart, Sen. Tim Scott, said when asked about a potential run. Scott escorted Graham during her swearing-in ceremony on July 14 at the U.S. Capitol in Washington.
President Trump endorses Darline Graham
The president said in his July 17 Truth Social post that he had given his "complete and total endorsement" to Graham.
"I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey," Trump wrote.
When Graham accepted her appointment to fill her brother’s Senate seat last week, she recalled their close relationship. Her brother adopted her after they lost both of their parents 15 months apart during her childhood.
"Lindsey has always been there for me," Graham said. "And now I will be there for him."
Graham is a married mother of two adult children and a grandmother of one who spent most of her professional career in disability services and workforce development.
Contributing: Jay Stahl, USA TODAY

sources.news_title: Sen. Darline Graham to Run for Full Term to Fill Brother’s Seat
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) is going to try to win an election to secure a full term in the U.S. Senate, she said July 20, after being named to fill the seat left vacant by her brother’s death.
“I’ve made a decision,” Graham, 62, said on Fox News. “I’m in.”
Lindsey Graham had been the Republican nominee for the seat in the upcoming November election, and his death triggered a special GOP primary to select a different GOP nominee.
Candidates can file to run in the special primary election between July 21 and July 28. The election will be held on the second Tuesday after July 28, or Aug. 11.
If needed, a primary runoff would take place two weeks later.
The general election this year is slated to take place on Nov. 3.
Candidates who say they’re running in the special primary include Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.), businessman Mark Lynch, and Rep. Russell Fry (R-S.C.).
Darline Graham told Fox News that she took the time to consider whether to enter the race.
“I have been praying a lot, talking to my family,” she said. “But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker—I learned that from Lindsey, he cared about the people of this state, I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state—I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes. Absolutely.”
Lindsey Graham had won the Republican primary earlier in the year with 263,895 votes. Lynch came in second with 134,246 votes.
Fry said earlier Monday that he would be “a conservative fighter in the Senate who delivers real results” if he wins the election.
Rep. Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) announced on Monday she is not running for Graham’s seat.
The Democratic nominee is Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician and mother who says she’s running for the Senate “because families are struggling in ways that we should never accept as normal.”

sources.news_title: Lindsey Graham’s sister running for a full term with Trump’s endorsement
Darline Graham tells Fox News 'I'm in,' will run for a full Senate term
sources.text:
Darline Graham tells Fox News 'I'm in,' will run for full Senate term
- Darline Graham, sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, announced she will run for a full Senate term.
- Graham's announcement came during an interview on Fox News with host Sean Hannity.
- President Donald Trump endorsed Graham for the Senate seat on July 17.
- Graham is currently serving an appointed term that was set to expire in January 2027.
Darline Graham, sister to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, said on July 20 that she will run for a full Senate term in the upcoming special election.
Graham, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump on July 17, told Fox News host Sean Hannity that she has been praying and talking to her family about the matter and has come to a decision. Graham is currently serving in the Senate after being appointed to the seat by Gov. Henry McMaster, but her term in office would have ended in January 2027.
"I've made a decision," Graham said. "I'm in."
Graham joins a field with several Republican candidates, including Greenville businessman Mark Lynch and U.S. Reps. Ralph Norman, District 5, and Russell Fry, District 7. Since Lindsey Graham won the Republican Senate primary before his death on July 11, there will be a special primary on Aug. 11 to determine his replacement as the party's nominee in the November general election. The winner will face Democrat Dr. Annie Andrews, a Charleston pediatrician.
U.S. Rep. Nancy Mace, R-District 1, who had been touted as a possible Senate candidate, said in a video announcement on July 20 that she will not be running for the Senate.
"I am not running for the U.S. Senate," Mace said. "Not because I'm backing down from a fight, but because the one I am already in matters right now."
The candidate filing period for the special primary will be open July 21-28. The candidates will appear on the August ballot.
Who is Darline Graham?
Darline Graham lives in Lexington, and she is married with two children and one grandchild. She started her career as a certified optician and has held various roles with Clemson University, the South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce and the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department. She also serves on the South Carolina State Workforce Development Board and is commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind.
Graham took a jump into politics when she was appointed to serve in the U.S. Senate by McMaster. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that he recommended Graham for the position.
"This would be a fabulous tribute to Lindsey, who loved her dearly," Trump wrote.
Trump later endorsed Graham in the Senate special primary before she formally announced her candidacy. The next day, she wrote an open letter to South Carolinians saying that it is time for her to "step up for South Carolina."
"I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things," Graham wrote. "But we were raised with the same values: work hard every day, trust in the lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for."
Bella Carpentier covers the South Carolina legislature, state, and Greenville County politics. Contact her at bcarpentier@gannett.com.

Darline Graham to run for full term to replace her brother in Senate
Washington — U.S. Senator Darline Graham said on Monday she plans to run for a full term to replace her brother, late Senator Lindsey Graham, who died this month after serving two decades in the U.S. Senate.
Last week, President Donald Trump asked her to run for the U.S. Senate in a special Republican primary in South Carolina on August 11. She was appointed to fill her brother's vacant Senate seat until the first week of January.
"I have been praying a lot, talking to my family … I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes. Absolutely," she told Fox News' 'Hannity' program in a clip released on Monday.
Lindsey Graham, a one-time vocal critic of Trump who went on to become one of the Republican president's staunchest allies, died on July 11 from a heart ailment caused by hardening of the arteries, his office said.
U.S. Representative Ralph Norman, a South Carolina Republican, said on Saturday he will seek to replace Lindsey Graham in the Senate.
Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the Senate and the House of Representatives heading into November's U.S. midterm elections.
The late U.S. senator's memorial will be held on July 28 in Washington and July 29 in South Carolina.
South Carolina's Republican Party will hold a special primary election on August 11 with a runoff on August 25 if no candidate wins a majority. Whoever captures the party nomination will face Democrat Annie Andrews in the November 3 general election.

‘I’m all in’: Senator Darline Graham enters race for U.S. Senate
COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - Sen. Darline Graham announced her run for a full term on Monday after being appointed to replace her late brother, Lindsey.
“The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina. I intend to earn every vote because that’s what this job demands, and that’s what the people of South Carolina deserve. Your concerns are my concerns. Your hopes for our state are my hopes as well. I’m ready for the fight ahead, and I’m all in,” Senator Graham said.
In a clip from an interview with Fox News’ Sean Hannity posted Monday, Graham said she was “in” when asked if she would consider a campaign.
“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family,” she said in part. “But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey. He cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state.”
“I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it,” she continued.
MORE COVERAGE
The news comes days after President Donald Trump offered his endorsement to Graham, who at that time had not publicly made a decision.
Four other candidates - U.S. Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman, as well as Duke Buckner and Mark Lynch - have each announced their intention to run in the August Republican primary.
Filing for the primary opens on July 21, with the primary scheduled for Aug. 11.

sources.news_title: Darline Graham to run for full term to replace her brother in U.S. Senate
Sen. Darline Graham running for full Senate term after being appointed to Lindsey Graham’s seat
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham announced that she will run for her late brother’s seat this November, after being appointed last week to serve out the rest of Lindsey Graham’s term.
“I’ve made a decision. I’m in,” she said in an interview with Sean Hannity on Fox News.
Graham acknowledged the “tremendous amount of pressure” she’s felt to make up her mind quickly, with a filing deadline looming and President Donald Trump posting on Truth Social that he would like her to run for the seat.
“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family, but with the love of my family, with the support of his staff — I know I’m a hard worker, I learned that from Lindsey,” she added. “He cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state. I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes, absolutely.”
Graham is the first woman to represent South Carolina in the Senate. She was appointed to the seat by South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster to serve until January 2027. A special primary election will take place August 11 to determine who will next hold the seat for the upcoming six-year term.
Multiple influential South Carolina Republicans told CNN the initial reports last week that Darline Graham planned to seek a full Senate term came as a surprise, as it was understood by them she would only complete the remainder of Lindsey Graham’s term.
A source with knowledge of the matter said that at the time McMaster appointed her to serve the remainder of her late brother’s current term, he was not under the impression Darline Graham would run as a candidate in the special primary election for a full term.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said on Monday that he is not endorsing Darline Graham at this time but called her “strong candidate.”
When asked by CNN why she is a strong candidate and what practical experience she brings to the job, Thune said: “She obviously carries on Lindsey’s legacy. But I think she’s a very accomplished person in her own right, and so you know she has a right, like anybody else, to get into that race.”
“It sounds like there are a number who are moving forward with campaigns. It’s going to be a short campaign season, I think, for the law in South Carolina, what it provides for,” Thune added. “But my assumption is that, you know, the voters in South Carolina, Republican voters, will come to a conclusion about that and send the right person forward.”
Senate GOP Whip John Barrasso, however, quickly backed Graham on Monday.
“Darline Graham is an excellent senator,” he told CNN. “She’ll continue to be an excellent senator, and she has my full support as she runs to fill the six-year term of Lindsey Graham.”
Graham, 62, has not previously held elected office. After she and Lindsey Graham’s parents died within 15 months of each other, she became orphaned at age 13 in 1976. Lindsey Graham — the first in his family to attend college, and a member of the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps — became his sister’s legal guardian.
South Carolina Rep. Russell Fry also announced on Monday he will join the race to replace Lindsey Graham in the Senate.
“We need a conservative fighter in the Senate who delivers real results. I will be your conservative MAGA candidate in the special primary Senate election this summer,” Fry wrote on X.
Fry’s announcement comes after widespread speculation that he would seek the open seat. A third-term congressman representing South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District, Fry rose to national prominence in 2022 when he defeated incumbent Rep. Tom Rice in a Republican primary after Rice voted to impeach President Donald Trump. Backed by Trump’s endorsement, Fry went on to win the general election, cementing his ties to the party’s MAGA wing.
Before endorsing Darline Graham, Trump had spoken highly of Fry as a potential person to watch in the special primary.
Fry and Graham join the race alongside South Carolina Rep. Ralph Norman, attorney Duke Buckner and businessman Mark Lynch. Filing officially opens July 21.
Rep. Nancy Mace, who failed to win the GOP nomination for South Carolina governor earlier this year, announced on Monday that she would not run for Graham’s seat.
Lindsey Graham, a longtime Republican from South Carolina and ally of President Donald Trump, died following an aortic dissection, according to a preliminary finding from the Washington, DC, medical examiner. He was 71.
This story has been updated with additional reporting.
CNN’s Richa Sharma contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Sen. Darline Graham says she is running for a full 6-year term after Trump urged her to jump into the race
sources.text:
Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., said she will run for a full term for the seat held by her late brother, Lindsey Graham, days after President Donald Trump said he urged her to jump into the race.
Graham said in an interview with Fox News’ Sean Hannity that she will run in next month’s special primary election to appear on the November ballot.
“I’ve made a decision,” Graham said in a clip released on X. “I’m in.”
“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family. But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey. He cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state,” Graham said. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes, absolutely.”
Trump on Friday said that he had given his “complete and total endorsement” to Graham, the younger sister of the late senator. “I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.
Graham was sworn in to the Senate seat last Tuesday, a day after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to the role to finish out her late brother’s term, which ends in early January. The elder Graham died July 11 at age 71 of what was preliminarily diagnosed as a rupture of his aorta due to a hardening of his arteries, his office said.
Graham’s funeral services are scheduled for July 28 in Washington, D.C., and July 29 in South Carolina.
Other GOP candidates who have announced plans to run in the Aug. 11 election include South Carolina Republican Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman and South Carolina businessman Mark Lynch, who lost to Lindsey Graham in the June Republican primary.
Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who ran an unsuccessful bid for South Carolina governor this year, said in a video statement Monday afternoon that she will not be seeking the Senate seat.
“I want to be straight with you. I’m not running for the U.S. Senate, not because I’m backing down from a fight, but because the one I’m already in matters now,” Mace said, referencing her legislative efforts on protecting women from sexual abuse.
“I’m not chasing another title, I’m chasing justice,” she added in her video, which was posted after Graham announced her candidacy.
The filing deadline for next month’s special election is July 28. The winner will go on to face Democrat Annie Andrews in November.
When she accepted her appointment to her brother’s seat last week, Darline Graham recounted their close relationship and said, “Lindsey has always been there for me, and now I will be there for him.”

Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham's sister, says she'll run for full Senate term
Washington — Sen. Darline Graham, who is serving out the remainder of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's term in the Senate, said Monday that she will seek a full term for the South Carolina seat her brother held for more than two decades.
"I've made a decision," Graham told Fox News. "I'm in."
The late senator, who died on July 11, had secured the GOP nomination in June for what would have been his fifth term representing South Carolina. With his death, the Republican candidate in the South Carolina Senate race will be determined by a special primary election. Republicans seeking the Senate seat may file between July 21 and July 28, before an Aug. 11 primary to decide who will take on Democrat Annie Andrews in November.
Graham, 62, was sworn in last week, after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to serve out the remainder of her brother's term, which runs through early January. Graham, who doesn't have a background in elected office, had a career in disabilities services and most recently served as commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind. She said upon accepting the appointment that finishing her brother's term "is what Lindsey would have wanted," noting that she planned to "honor him in this way."
President Trump publicly encouraged Graham to run for a six-year term, writing in a post on Truth Social after meeting with her at the White House last week that she would have his "Complete and Total Endorsement."
"I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey," Mr. Trump said.
In an interview with Fox News' Sean Hannity, Graham said, "I have been praying a lot, talking to my family."
"I know I'm a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey," she said. "I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes. Absolutely."
The president's endorsement hasn't stopped other Republicans from announcing their intention to run for the six-year term. Rep. Ralph Norman, who's represented South Carolina in the House since 2017, announced a bid on Saturday. And Rep. Russell Fry, who was elected to the House in 2022, announced his candidacy on Monday.
If no candidate secures a majority of the vote in the special primary election, a runoff will be held on Aug. 25.
